From: Maya Ghosh <maya@ledgerpay.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency / retention clarification for Dedicated deployment

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal and security teams need a few concrete confirmations before we can move forward with a Dedicated contract. Please do not escalate to marketing — these are technical questions for the deployment/ops side. High-level summary: LedgerPay requires that customer data for a dedicated tenant never leaves the contracted US region, and that deletion requests (including backups and snapshots) are honored within a bounded time window.

Can you confirm the following for a Dedicated deployment on your US cluster?

1) At-rest: Are both active data and backups (snapshots, object-store copies) confined to the same physical region? If replication is used for availability, how is cross-region replication prevented?
2) Network egress: Is there any control plane traffic (logs, metrics, autoscaling telemetry) that can contain or transmit customer data outside the region?
3) Purge SLA: If LedgerPay issues a tenant deletion, what is the end-to-end window for removing active writes, KV caches, user-index snapshots, and cold backups (including any S3-style artifacts)?
4) Evidence: We will need a short attestation and an OPS playbook snippet that shows the deletion runbook for a Dedicated tenant (high level).

Appreciate a clear, actionable response we can share with our InfoSec. If you prefer we can set up a quick call with your ops team today.

Best,
Maya
Maya Ghosh
Head of Security Operations
LedgerPay

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear list. I can answer some items and will confirm the exact SLAs with our Ops team (cc'd). Short answers here and a plan for next steps below.

- At-rest: Yes — Dedicated tenants are deployed onto region-specific pools and attached block/object storage remains within that region. We do not perform automatic cross-region replication for Dedicated customers unless explicitly configured and contracted.

- Network egress: The control plane collects health and anonymized metrics. No customer payloads are forwarded outside the region by default. There are a few metrics/logs that reference tenant IDs for observability; those are scrubbed to prevent sensitive content transfer.

- Purge SLA: I will confirm the end-to-end deletion window (including backups) with Ops.

- Evidence: We can provide a one-page attestation and a redacted snippet of the tenant deletion playbook.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm the canonical deletion workflow and provide an expected max timeline for: active data deletion, KV cache eviction, snapshot tombstone + eventual object-store deletion, and confirmation artifacts we can share? Laure — can you add any contract language notes we should include for LP-3427?

Maya — I can host a 30-minute call with Ben and Laura today or tomorrow to walk through the playbook and the artifacts. What works for you?

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency / retention clarification for Dedicated deployment

Jordan / Laura — answering inline below. Quoted Maya's original at the bottom for traceability.

1) At-rest: Confirmed. Dedicated runs use region-scoped storage classes. Backups (snapshots) are taken locally in-region into our object store buckets that are tagged with a regional policy. We only create cross-region replicas for disaster recovery if the customer signs a DR addendum (explicit opt-in).

2) Network egress: Control plane telemetry includes bucket sizes, instance health, and anonymized error traces; we do not ship raw user payloads. We also run egress filters and a data-loss prevention (DLP) hook on export interfaces that prevent scheduled exports from transferring content fields.

3) Purge SLA: Proposed operational windows — these are conservative and include manual verification steps: 
- Active writes & indexes: within 4 hours of an authenticated tenant deletion request.
- KV caches / in-memory state: evicted immediately on delete command; fully flushed within 30 minutes for idle caches.
- Snapshots / object-store artifacts: tombstone initiated within 1 hour, and object deletions completed within 7 days (object-store garbage-collection windows and backup lifecycle depend on provider-level retention). We can shorten the object deletion window to 72 hours under contract (e.g., commit in SLA) if LedgerPay requires it.

4) Evidence / playbook: Attached two artifacts we can share internally: (1) a one-page residency matrix (redwood-dedicated-residency-matrix.pdf) summarizing where each artifact lives, and (2) an ops snippet (ops-playbook-snippet.txt) showing the deletion checklist and verification commands. We will redact internal hostnames.

Notes on guarantees: We can provide an attestation letter stating that "no automatic cross-region replication occurs by default for Dedicated customers and deletion processes are executed as described." For legal purposes, the deletion timeline for object-store items can be narrowed with an SLA commitment and contractual language; otherwise provider GC windows apply.

Let me know if you want me to join a call with LedgerPay.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Infrastructure Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
